sections.h2: Ways to sell in East Orange
sections.html:
East Orange owners generally pick among a listing, a private sale, and a direct cash purchase. Listing brings the most buyers, but here the paperwork often decides the closing date. The city requires a Certificate of Conformity before a property is sold, and the fire department issues a smoke alarm and carbon monoxide certificate for one and two family homes. Both take scheduling.

  • Agent listing: fits a house that can clear the city's certificate inspections with little work.
  • Cash purchase: fits an inherited or tenant-occupied house, or one carrying open code violations.
  • Private sale: still needs the Certificate of Conformity, a deed, and the state's seller forms.

East Orange is a dense city, with an estimated 72,159 residents on 3.93 square miles. Owners live in just 31.0 percent of homes, so rentals make up a big slice of the stock. The middle value of an owned home is $365,900, against $454,400 across New Jersey, and median gross rent is $1,441. The city sits in Essex County beside Newark, South Orange, Orange, Glen Ridge and Bloomfield.

Buyers often ask for a neighborhood by name: Ampere in the northeast, Greenwood (the Teen Streets), Presidential Estates in the north with its larger homes, and Elmwood in the southeast around Elmwood Park.

East Orange has two commuter rail stops, East Orange and Brick Church, both on NJ Transit's Morris and Essex Lines with daily trains to New York Penn Station and weekday trains to Hoboken. The East Orange station sits beside Interstate 280, directly across a parking lot from City Hall. More than a dozen NJ Transit bus routes, including the 5, 21, 24, 34, 41, 44, 71, 73, 79, 90, 92, 94 and 97, cover the city.

By road, the Garden State Parkway is reached at Interchange 145 for I-280 and Interchange 147 for Springdale Avenue. The average commute is 35.4 minutes, so naming the nearest station in a listing helps.

sections.h2: What is a Certificate of Conformity?
sections.html:
It is the city's pre-sale compliance certificate. Under Section 159-50, it must be in hand before a property is sold. It shows the property conforms to the city code, and the code holds seller and buyer both accountable for getting it. Apply in person at the Department of Property Maintenance, East Orange City Hall, 44 City Hall Plaza, third floor, paying by certified check or money order, since no cash is taken. The phone is 973-266-5320.

After an inspection, the city mails a Notice of Code Violations listing everything found and a correction deadline. Items left uncorrected can bring a summons and fines between $100 and $2,000 per offense. Ask Code Enforcement whether any open notices sit on your house before you list it.

sections.h2: Smoke alarm and carbon monoxide certificate
sections.html:
For a one or two family home, the Fire Department issues a Certificate of Smoke Alarm and Carbon Monoxide Compliance. Ask the buyer's attorney whether it is expected at your closing. Call the Fire Prevention Bureau at 973-266-5520 to book, at least a day ahead. Appointments run Monday to Thursday between 9 and 3. One and two family homes can also get free smoke detector installation from the city.

East Orange detector certificate fees
Booking lead timeFee
Ten or more business days ahead$100
Four to nine business days ahead$125
One to three business days ahead$175
Failed inspection, re-inspection or no-show$50

Planning pays: a booking made one to three days out costs $75 more than one made ten business days out.

sections.h2: Other items that come up at closing
sections.html:
• Water, sewer and refuse: owners are responsible for charges run up by tenants, and a property that owes money at the end of the prior calendar year is included in that year's tax lien sale. Call the Water Department at 973-266-8869 for a final reading and balance.
  • Service line: the piece beyond the curb box belongs to the owner, so a leak there is the owner's repair.
  • Superintendent license: a building with four or more dwelling units needs a designated, registered superintendent, renewed yearly.
  • Lead paint: the state inspection law applies to rentals built before 1978 and not to home sales, but federal rules still require a seller to disclose known lead hazards in a pre-1978 home.

The state's realty transfer fee is the seller's cost, charged on a schedule by price. Senior, blind or disabled sellers and certain affordable housing sales use a lower schedule. Your attorney or title agent can work out the figure for your price.

The Essex County Register of Deeds and Mortgages files East Orange deeds. It occupies Room 130 of the Hall of Records, 465 Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard in Newark, takes its last transaction at 4:15 on weekdays, and answers at 973-621-4960. A certified deed copy costs $8 for page one and $2 for each page after, and the staff will not conduct title searches.

For an East Orange sale, start with the city, not the buyer. Call Code Enforcement to learn whether any Notice of Code Violations is open, then apply for the Certificate of Conformity at City Hall. Book the fire department detector appointment next, aiming for ten or more business days before closing to get the lowest fee. Ask the Water Department for a balance so nothing lands on the tax lien list, and tell your attorney about any tenants, since a building with four or more units adds the superintendent registration question.

A cash buyer can take the house as it stands and adjust the offer for open violations. A buyer using a mortgage will usually want them cleared before closing.

On the day of the closing, expect the title agent or attorney to ask for the Certificate of Conformity, the detector certificate where it applies, a final water balance, and your payoff letter. Having each of these in a single folder, with the Property Maintenance and Fire Prevention phone numbers written on the front, saves a scramble if a buyer's attorney asks a question late. Call the Fire Prevention Bureau again if the date moves, since the lead-time fee depends on how many business days remain. Sellers who inherited the house should also bring the estate papers so the attorney can confirm who has authority to sign the deed and the seller's tax form.

faqs.q: Is a Certificate of Conformity mandatory for an East Orange sale?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires it before a property is sold, and the code makes both seller and buyer responsible for obtaining it. Apply in person at the Department of Property Maintenance, third floor of City Hall.

faqs.q: What does the East Orange fire department charge for the detector certificate?
faqs.a: It is $100 with ten or more business days of notice, $125 with four to nine, and $175 with one to three. A failed inspection or a missed appointment costs $50.

faqs.q: Can a house with open code violations be sold in East Orange?
faqs.a: Yes. The violations stay with the property, and the owner receives a Notice of Code Violations with a deadline. A cash buyer can accept the house as it stands and adjust the offer for the open items.

faqs.q: Does the state lead paint inspection law reach home sales?
faqs.a: No, it covers rentals built before 1978. Federal law still requires a seller to disclose known lead hazards in a house older than 1978.

faqs.q: Which office files an East Orange deed?
faqs.a: The Essex County Register of Deeds and Mortgages in Newark, reachable at 973-621-4960. The seller's tax form goes with the deed, and the transfer fee is the seller's.
